tasks.short: Search earlier lab work, design experiments, run trial formulations and method tests, record results, and decide the next trial.

steps.what: Chemist searches earlier lab work and literature for the product or method
Chemist designs experiments to develop or improve formulas, processes or analytical methods
Chemist runs trial formulations and method tests in the lab
Chemist records results in a paper notebook and a spreadsheet
Chemist evaluates results and decides the next trial

tasks.design: Trials are recorded in an electronic lab notebook ({DATA_PLATFORM}) that imports instrument results and links each trial to its formula and conditions, so results are not copied from paper into spreadsheets. Earlier experiments are searchable by ingredient, method and outcome. Designing experiments, running trials and deciding the next step stay with the chemist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Results sat in paper notebooks and personal spreadsheets that colleagues could not search.
tasks.enabler_now: Electronic lab notebooks import instrument data and index experiments.
tasks.still_hard: Old paper notebooks are not in the index.
tasks.human_edge: Sensing why a formula separates when the numbers look fine.

reach.learn: Whether method details are complete at transfer.

evidence.claim: Electronic lab notebooks can import instrument data and make earlier experiments searchable.
Audit trails naming staff are personal data; works council consent is needed if used to check performance.

assumptions: Boundary: from the development brief to the next trial decided; scale-up is outside.
Input contract: instruments export data; fallback is paper and spreadsheets.
Designing and running trials do not change.
research_questions: Do repeated trials fall when earlier work is searchable?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few trials; high: many short trials with instrument data.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Log samples, prepare them, run chromatography or spectroscopy, interpret the results, transfer results and check them against specifications, and sign them off.

steps.what: Chemist logs incoming samples on paper
Chemist prepares samples for analysis
Chemist analyzes compounds using chromatography, spectroscopy or spectrophotometry
Chemist interprets chromatograms and spectra to determine composition and structure
Chemist copies results into a spreadsheet and checks them against specifications
Chemist signs off the results

tasks.design: Samples are logged with barcodes in a laboratory information system ({DATA_PLATFORM}). Results from the chromatography and spectroscopy software are imported into the sample record, and fixed rules check them against the specification and flag deviations, instead of copying into a spreadsheet. Preparing samples, running instruments, interpreting spectra and signing off stay with the chemist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Samples were logged on paper and results copied into spreadsheets for checking.
tasks.enabler_now: Laboratory systems import instrument results and check specifications.
tasks.still_hard: Older instruments do not export data cleanly.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising a contaminant peak that the method does not expect.
tasks.altitude: The chemist reviews flagged deviations instead of copying results.

evidence.claim: An Irish ISO 17025 water testing lab replaced paper and spreadsheet processes with an Instem laboratory system.
Draft GMP Annex 22 says generative AI should not be used in critical GMP applications; here only fixed rules check specifications.

assumptions: Boundary: from samples received to results signed; batch release is outside.
Input contract: instruments connected to the laboratory system; fallback is paper and spreadsheets.
Interpretation and sign-off stay with the chemist.
Computer system validation is done before use.
research_questions: Do transcription errors found at review fall?

incremental.description: Chemist enters results from unconnected instruments by hand.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few samples with complex analyses; high: many routine samples.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Set up reactions with heat, light or catalysts, run and monitor them, record reaction conditions, and judge the outcome.

steps.what: Chemist sets up reactions introducing heat, light, energy or chemical catalysts
Chemist runs and monitors the reactions to induce changes in composition
Chemist records temperatures, times and amounts by hand
Chemist judges the outcome for quantitative or qualitative analysis

tasks.design: Heating blocks, reactors and balances log temperatures, times and weights directly into the electronic lab notebook ({DATA_PLATFORM}), so the chemist does not write them down. Setting up and monitoring reactions and judging the outcome stay with the chemist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Conditions were written by hand from displays.
tasks.enabler_now: Lab equipment can log conditions into electronic notebooks.
tasks.still_hard: Older equipment has no data output.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing a colour change that means the reaction went wrong.

evidence.claim: Lab equipment such as balances and reactors can log conditions into electronic notebooks.

assumptions: Boundary: from the reaction plan to the outcome judged; analysis of products is outside.
Input contract: equipment with data output; fallback is writing by hand.
Setting up and monitoring do not change.
research_questions: Are reaction records complete more often?

incremental.description: Chemist enters conditions from unconnected equipment.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly old equipment; high: connected reactors and balances.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather test results, make charts and tables, write the technical report or specification, check it with a second chemist, and release it in the document system.

steps.what: Chemist gathers test results from spreadsheets and lab records
Chemist makes charts and tables
Chemist writes technical reports or prepares standards and specifications for products or tests

loop.input: A fixed evidence pack: the results, charts, tables, method references and the template for the report or specification.
loop.output: A draft report or specification in the template.
loop.check: Code checks every number and reference in the draft against the evidence pack and stops on any miss; the chemist rewrites and approves.
loop.stop: Stops on the first number or reference not in the pack; after two failed drafts the chemist writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Discussion and rationale are prose; a template fills only the tables.

steps.what: Chemist checks the final report with a second chemist
Chemist e-mails the report to the document controller for release

tasks.design: Results come from the laboratory system ({DATA_PLATFORM}) into a fixed evidence pack, and scripted pipelines make the charts and tables, so nothing is copied by hand. A bounded step drafts the report or specification from the pack; code checks every number and reference against the pack and stops on any miss. The chemist rewrites the discussion and a second chemist checks it; once checked, it enters the document system's release workflow. In GMP labs, specifications are written by the chemist without the drafting step.
tasks.previous_blocker: Results were gathered from spreadsheets and reports written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Laboratory systems export results; language models draft from a fixed pack that code can check.
tasks.still_hard: Models invent references unless every one is checked.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a specification limit the plant can actually meet.
tasks.altitude: The chemist rewrites and checks instead of compiling.

reach.learn: Whether reports arrive with checked numbers.

evidence.claim: In 84 generated literature reviews, 55% of GPT-3.5 and 18% of GPT-4 references were fabricated.
Draft GMP Annex 22 says generative AI and LLMs should not be used in critical GMP applications.

assumptions: Boundary: from the report request to the report released; customer use is outside.
Input contract: results in the laboratory system; fallback is spreadsheets.
The chemist and a second chemist check every report.
GMP specifications are not drafted by the model.
research_questions: How often does the check stop a draft?

incremental.description: Chemist keeps chart scripts and templates current.

approvals.approved_version: The report as checked with a second chemist in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: GMP specifications written by hand; high: routine test reports.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The chemist keeps designing experiments, running analyses and reactions, interpreting results and setting specifications; paper notebooks, spreadsheet copying and report compiling shrink.
skills_to_grow: Checking drafted reports against the evidence pack
role.ambitious_version: A chemist with more time at the bench.
